data.name: New Caledonia
data.summary: New Caledonia has its own tax code, separate from France. Private investors' gains on securities are generally untaxed; only real estate gains are taxed (24%). Dividends from local companies bear a 20% final withholding. Foreign dividends appear to fall into progressive income tax, up to 40%. There is no wealth tax. Inheritances and gifts to children are taxed at 5%-20% on worldwide assets when the deceased was resident.

regimes.name: Tax domicile in New Caledonia
regimes.description: Residents pay progressive personal income tax (0-40%) on worldwide income, with family quotient splitting capped at XPF 300,000 of savings.
regimes.eligibility: Tax domicile under the local code: home or principal place of stay, main professional activity, or centre of economic interests in New Caledonia.

capital_gains.summary: Capital gains of individuals are generally not taxable. Exception: private real estate gains (PVI) are taxed at 20% plus 4% CCS (24% in total), with exemptions and special rules.

capital_gains.rate_basis: PwC (reviewed 9 Sep 2026): 'Capital gains derived by individuals are generally not taxable', except real estate (PVI 20% + CCS 4%). Securities and private business shares 0. Real estate 0.24 is the headline before any holding-period relief (relief not researched). Foreign real estate assumed outside PVI.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Habitual trading could be business income under the progressive scale; not researched.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: No tax on gains from foreign securities found.

dividends.summary: Dividends from New Caledonian companies bear 20% at source (IRVM 11.5% + CCS 4% + additional centimes 4.5%) and are not subject to personal income tax. Foreign dividends are not covered by IRVM and appear to be taxed in personal income tax at progressive rates up to 40%, with a foreign tax credit.

dividends.rate_basis: Domestic: 0.20 final (PwC income determination; DSF IRVM page 'total de 20%'). Foreign: residents are taxed on worldwide income at 0-40% (PwC), and IRVM applies only to distributions by companies with their seat in New Caledonia (DSF), so foreign dividends are assumed to fall into the progressive scale at the 40% top rate. PwC mentions foreign tax credits. Low confidence for foreign dividends.
dividends.withholding_outbound: Dividends paid to non-residents: about 20% for individuals, 21% for companies (IRVM + CCS + centimes, plus possibly CAIS 3%); France-New Caledonia treaty: 15% individuals, 5% companies.
dividends.treaty_network: Only one comprehensive treaty, with France (1983). No treaty with the US or other EU states.
dividends.holding_company_notes: IRVM reinvestment reduction (art. Lp 543.2-I) for local reinvestment; not relevant to a foreign portfolio.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Contribution foncière on land and buildings, computed from surface area times a rate per m2 and then 8.4% (buildings) or 0.7875% (land), varying by commune (PwC).

inheritance.summary: Inheritance and gift duties are charged on each beneficiary. If the deceased or donor was resident in New Caledonia, worldwide assets are taxed; otherwise only New Caledonian assets. Children: progressive rates of 5% to 20% after an allowance of XPF 100,000. Spouses and PACS partners are exempt. Modelled as 20% on everything above XPF 100,000 per child.

open_questions: The band thresholds of the 5%-20% direct-line scale were not found (code des impôts art. 248-417 not reachable); the JSON applies 20% to the whole amount above the allowance, an upper bound that is close for a EUR 11.7M share per child.
PwC's wording of the XPF 100,000 allowance ('when beneficiaries are direct dependants (spouse or partner…)') is ambiguous.
Any lifetime gift recall period not researched.
inheritance.spouse_note: PwC states that no inheritance tax is due between spouses or PACS partners; its separate line giving a XPF 100,000 allowance and 5%-20% rates for 'direct dependants (spouse or partner)' is ambiguous, and the local Code des impots (arts. 248-417) could not be opened, so confidence is medium.
inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts follow the same rules as inheritances 'but some differences could exist' (PwC).
inheritance.foreign_assets: Worldwide assets when the deceased/donor is a tax resident of New Caledonia; local assets only otherwise.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Based on the tax domicile of the deceased or donor in New Caledonia.

residency.tax_residency_test: Domicile if any of: home or principal place of stay in New Caledonia, main professional activity there, or centre of economic interests there. The France-New Caledonia treaty has tie-breakers (permanent home, vital interests, habitual abode).

routes.name: French citizens
routes.requirements: French citizens can settle freely. Other EU citizens: entry and residence follow French immigration rules specific to New Caledonia (not researched).

routes.name: Non-French citizens: residence permit
routes.requirements: Long stays need a visa and a residence card under the immigration rules applicable in New Caledonia (details not researched).

corporate.summary: CIT 30% (15% for smaller companies below turnover thresholds; 35% mining and metallurgy), plus CAIS 3% on distributions above XPF 30M and an additional social contribution of 5%-15% for large profits. Taxed on New Caledonian-source income.

data.us_citizen_notes: No US-New Caledonia tax treaty; US citizens would pay New Caledonian tax plus US federal tax, with foreign tax credits on the US side.

Foreign dividends: progressive-scale treatment assumed, not confirmed.

succession.name: New Caledonia
succession.summary: French civil law applies, so children have a protected share (the réserve) that a will cannot cut. People with Kanak customary status follow custom on customary land. A foreign resident cannot choose their national law, and the EU Succession Regulation does not apply. The Hague Trusts Convention is not in force for France.
succession.reserved_share: Children: 1/2 with one child, 2/3 with two, 3/4 with three or more (Code civil art 913); if no descendants, a surviving spouse 1/4 (art 914-1). Applies outside customary land and to persons under common-law civil status.
succession.foreign_law_note: The EU Succession Regulation does not apply in New Caledonia (an overseas country and territory). Under French common-law conflict rules, land follows the law of its location and movables the last domicile, so a resident cannot select national law (not verified from a New Caledonia source).
succession.trust_note: The fiducie (Code civil arts 2011 ff.) is a statutory trust with narrow uses; its extension to New Caledonia was not verified. Foreign trusts: France has signed but not ratified the Convention. Foundations: only charitable forms (fondations, fonds de dotation) are known in France; local availability not verified.
open_questions: Whether fiducie and fondation law extend to New Caledonia (civil law was transferred to the territory in 2013).
Whether Code civil arts 912-914 apply unchanged locally.
The 2021 compensatory-levy rule (art 913) in this territory.
The HCCH table as retrieved shows no entry for this jurisdiction (the retrieved copy was marked last updated 2017 and its territorial-extension notes could not be read); re-check the live table.
